styleSelection.reason: Sargent's White Ships (1908) is a pure transparent watercolor built from luminous warm cream/ochre timber washes, cool cerulean-ultramarine shadow planes on the curved white hulls, soft turquoise-green and golden-amber water reflections, and crisp dark sienna-ultramarine accents for hawseholes, anchors, and shaded hull crevices, with organic unpainted paper whites reserved naturally and no ink linework.

families.name: Sunlit cream and golden-ochre hull planking, masts, and spar highlights
families.Role: broad light foundation wash across the sunlit hull planking, upper rigging spars, and warm bowsprit timber

families.name: Cool cerulean and lavender-grey shadow planes on the white ship hulls
families.Role: broad turning shadow washes across the central and left white hulls and upper-right rigging

families.name: Turquoise-slate and sea-green harbor water and lower hull reflection
families.Role: cool blue-green harbor water washes and reflected light under the bows

families.name: Warm yellow-ochre and raw-sienna deck structures, spars, and sunlit reflections
families.Role: saturated golden-ochre timber bands, deckhouse framing, bow scroll ornament, and warm amber water ripples

families.name: Burnt-sienna and mahogany shaded timber, rust streaks, and dark hull bands
families.Role: rich warm darks along the left hull shadow, anchor chains, rigging blocks, and lower hull waterline

families.name: Deep ultramarine-umber hawseholes, anchor shadows, and inter-hull crevices
families.Role: crisp darkest accents for the hawseholes, anchors, deep hull clefts, and dark reflection bands
